Ronald Levine | footnotes=???}} '''Mr. Backlot''' (Japanese: '''ウラヤマ''' ''Urayama'') is the owner of the {{si|Pokémon Mansion}} and [[Trophy Garden]]. He is also said to be the owner of [[Amity Square]]. His house has a back garden where {{Player}}s can catch [[wild Pokémon]]. He is apparently a compulsive liar, as he will repeatedly insist that a Pokémon appears in his garden despite not even [[List of Pokémon by Sinnoh Pokédex number|residing in his region]]. His butler, who serves him well, covers up for his lies, importing said Pokémon into the garden and allowing the player to catch rare Pokémon not found elsewhere in Sinnoh. This is often very helpful in completing the [[National Pokédex]]. ==In the core series games== Mr. Backlot is said to be the owner of {{si|Pokémon Mansion}}, the [[Trophy Garden]] behind it, and [[Amity Square]]. He resides in his office of the Pokémon Mansion, accompanied by his butler, and a guard. He takes a walk in his garden every morning, and discovers a new Pokémon everyday, surprising his butler. After saying that he is telling the truth about seeing the Pokémon, the butler leaves to add the Pokémon to the garden to cover up for his master's fibs. On any given day, the "planted" Pokémon that was in the Trophy Garden the previous time Mr. Backlot was last spoken with will also still be there, allowing a two-day window to catch each of these Pokémon. ===Quotes=== ;Pokémon Mansion :''"Er-hem! {{color2|000|Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl|Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl}} |} ==In animation== Mr. Backlot's only appearance in animation was in the {{aniseries|DP}} episode ''[[DP084|Hungry for the Good Life!]]''. Mr. Backlot welcomed {{Ash}} and {{ashfr}} into his mansion to escape a raging storm. The next day, Mr. Backlot took the group out to his [[Trophy Garden]] for the Pokémon to play. After {{TRT}} arrived with their [[Team Rocket's mechas|mecha]] and stole the Pokémon, Mr. Backlot and Monica drove Ash and {{an|Brock}} directly to the trio. {{an|Dawn}} eventually found Team Rocket and defeated them just as Mr. Backlot and others caught up. After Team Rocket was defeated, Mr. Backlot was happily reunited with his Pokémon. Everyone returned to the mansion to wave goodbye to the group and the {{TP|Dawn|Swinub}} that Dawn {{pkmn2|caught}}. Mr. Backlot amassed his collection of Pokémon from across the {{pkmn|world}}. He relies heavily on his housekeeper, {{OBP|Monica|DP084}}, for domestic chores like cooking and she also takes care of his mansion estate and Pokémon. Mr. Backlot was generous with his time and had Monica bring out [[Poffin]]s for the group's Pokémon during their stay. None of Pichu's moves are known.}} ====Seen at his garden==== {| width="100%" |- | {{InactivePoké|Mr. Backlot|Kricketune|Mr Backlot Kricketune Pikachu Adventures.png|Bug|link=no}} | {{InactivePoké|Mr. Backlot|Pikachu|Mr Backlot Kricketune Pikachu Adventures.png|Electric|link=no}} ♂ | {{InactivePoké|Mr. Backlot|Pichu|Mr Backlot Kricketune Pikachu Adventures.png|Electric|link=no}} | {{InactivePoké|Mr. Backlot|Roselia|Mr Backlot Roselia Adventures.png|Grass|Poison|link=no}} |- | {{InactivePoké|Mr. Backlot|Starly|Mr Backlot Starly Adventures.png|Normal|Flying|link=no}} |} ==Trivia== * Mr. Backlot's Japanese name is a pun. His name is "Urayama" (ウラヤマ), but his butler adds ''shi'' (し or 氏, which in this case is a more polite form of "Mr.") to his name, making his name sound like the Japanese word for being envious, 羨ましい (''urayamashii''). In the game, he asks the player "Well? Aren't you envious?" (どう？うらやましいじゃろ？？) over and over before telling the player what new Pokémon are in his garden. * In [[Pokémon X and Y]], Elena, who trades an {{p|Eevee}} nicknamed Stevie to the player for any Pokémon in a random [[Kalos hotels|hotel]], refers to Stevie as "Mr. Backlot's Pokémon" after the trade. * Swinub was the only one of Mr. Backlot's Pokémon shown in the anime that cannot appear in the Trophy Garden in-game. ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{normal color}}; border:3px solid #{{normal color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{normal color light}}" | Language ! style="background:#{{normal color light}}" | Name ! style="background:#{{normal color light}}" | Origin |- | Japanese | ウラヤマ ''Urayama'' | From 裏山 ''urayama'' (mountain or hill behind a house) and 羨ましい ''urayamashii'' (envious) |- | English | Mr. Backlot | From ''{{wp|backlot}}'' |- | German | Herr Reichedel | From ''reich'' (rich) and ''edel'' (noble) |- | rowspan = "2" | European Spanish | Señor Fortuny | From ''fortuna'' (fortune) |- | Señor Backlot[[Pokémon animated series]] | rowspan = "3" | From his English name |- | Latin American Spanish | Señor Backlot |- | Brazilian Portuguese | Senhor Backlot |- | French | M.
